answer: Pedal, then piston, then brake fluid, then the brake line (pressure), then the caliper (with its pistons), then the pads, which press on the disc at the wheel.
Because fluid can't be squeezed, so the pressure travels down the lines to every wheel.

Two pads were drawn side by side with a gap between them, stacked in a row under the caliper and above the disc, not on either side of the disc. The picture never showed the pads closing onto the disc.
Into heat: friction turns the car's motion into heat.
Far: the pedal box is at the top of the screen and the wheel circle is in the lower part, with empty space between them.
A box labelled CALIPER (with pistons) at the end of the brake line, above the wheel.
The disc, filled pink/salmon with the word HEAT under it.
